citation_context: L71: Cosmological ``dark energy'' is usually introduced as an additional component in the stress--energy budget of an otherwise homogeneous Friedmann--Lema\^{i}tre--Robertson--Walker (FLRW) universe. Empirically, the case for late-time acceleration is established by comparing model-predicted distance measures and clustering statistics to survey data products, and the resulting minimal phenomenological description is $\Lambda$CDM \cite{Riess1998SN,Perlmutter1999SN,Weinberg2013Acceleration}. The conceptual step that often remains implicit is that the fitted homogeneous description is treated as a closed macro-dynamical system: the model is evolved forward in time at the macro level, and its predictions are compared directly to observations. This paper asks what is required for that ``macro closure'' step to be justified, and what it means when it fails. Six Birds Theory (SBT) provides a vocabulary designed for precisely this situation: modeling a system that is observed only through a coarse interface. In SBT, a theory is not just a dynamical law; it is a closure package consisting of (i) a lens $\Lens:\StateSpace\to\ObsSpace$ specifying what is retained, (ii) a completion $\Completion:\ObsSpace\to\StateSpace$ specifying how discarded information is filled in, and (iii) audits that test whether the induced macro description is coherent under evolution \cite{Tsiokos2026SixBirds,Tsiokos2026WakeStone}. The associated packaging operator $\PackageOp= \Completion\circ \Lens$ is intended to be idempotent and to define the ``objects'' at the macro level. A central SBT diagnostic is route mismatch: if $T$ denotes time evolution on $\StateSpace$, then in general \begin{equation} \PackageOp\circ T \;\neq\; T\circ \PackageOp, || L93: We make the following concrete, falsifiable contributions: \begin{enumerate} \item \textbf{Closure-first formulation of dark energy.} We restate cosmological inference as a packaging problem involving a lens, a completion, and an induced packaging operator, and we identify route mismatch as the mechanism that forces operator rewrite terms at the macro level \cite{Tsiokos2026SixBirds,Tsiokos2026WakeStone}. \item \textbf{A reproducible computational and audit toolkit.} We implement a minimal API for lenses, completions, packaging, route mismatch, and idempotence defects, together with run manifests, provenance, and PPD-style cross-probe audits that standardize evidence reporting across experiments. \item \textbf{Mechanism and inference demonstrations.} We provide toy nonlinear and patch-cosmology proxies in which coarse-graining generates mismatch and an effective acceleration proxy; we also show, with synthetic distance--redshift data, that a null-$\Lambda$ heterogeneous generator can be mis-fit by a homogeneous $\Lambda$CDM model, yielding $\Omega_\Lambda>0$ as a closure-induced inference artifact. || L108: \section{Six Birds framework for cosmology}\label{sec:framework} This section summarizes the minimal Six Birds Theory (SBT) primitives we use throughout the paper and fixes notation. We follow the closure-first formulation in \cite{Tsiokos2026SixBirds,Tsiokos2026WakeStone}: a macro description is not merely a reduced state; it is the output of an explicit \emph{packaging} operator induced by an observational interface (lens) and a modeling assumption (completion). Route mismatch (non-commutation) is the key diagnostic that forces operator rewrites when a closed homogeneous macro theory does not descend.

citation_context: L73: \section{Introduction} \emph{Six Birds Theory} (SBT) is a closure-based emergence calculus introduced in~\cite{Tsiokos2026SixBirds}; readers unfamiliar with its primitives will find all required definitions self-contained in Section~\ref{sec:sbt}. This paper presents original computational results, mechanized proofs, and reproducible experiments that instantiate the SBT packaging language in the quantum domain. Quantum mechanics is our most accurate framework for microscopic phenomena, yet its standard presentation invites persistent conceptual puzzles: the state vector appears to collapse discontinuously upon measurement; entanglement correlations are often described as ``spooky action at a distance''; and Schr\"odinger's cat seems to demand macroscopic superpositions of mutually exclusive realities. Much of the interpretational debate concerns what the quantum state \emph{is}---a real physical field, an element of reality, or a bookkeeping device---but typically proceeds within a formalism that conflates causal claims about the world with inferential bookkeeping about what can be recorded. || L79: Following Spekkens, we take seriously the possibility that this is a category mistake.\cite{Spekkens2007Toy} The quantum state is a tool for prediction under limited access; elevating it to an ontic object tends to force ``surplus'' structure (e.g., influences that cannot be used to signal and that never appear in any admissible record). This clashes with a Leibnizian methodological principle: if two scenarios are empirically indiscernible at a given descriptive layer, then they should not be treated as distinct objects of reality at that layer. We argue that SBT provides a suitable replacement language.\cite{Tsiokos2026SixBirds} It explicitly separates causal substrate dynamics from \emph{packaging} operations that stabilize some distinctions into record-level objects. In this view, ``collapse'' is not a dynamical discontinuity but an idempotent packaging map (a closure) induced by a chosen record algebra; incompatibility of measurement contexts manifests as noncommuting closures (route mismatch), not superluminal causation; and the cat paradox is localized: ``alive vs.\ dead'' becomes an object-level distinction only when a stable record is packaged.\footnote{Reproducibility: all figures and quoted numbers are generated by \texttt{python -m sbtq.run\_all --seed 0 --out artifacts}; see Appendix~\ref{app:repro}.} \paragraph{Contributions.} || L170: This section fixes notation for the rest of the paper. licensed_conclusion: This paper isolates a control-stable intrinsic family inside the fixed-support recombination layer of Six Birds theory. The first three papers of the series established admissible event packages on fixed support, predictive quotients on single histories, and the branchwise and recombination quotients on branch assemblages. Here we identify a two-anchor relative-cycle family in which branchwise predictive agreement does not determine later recombination observables. We instantiate the standard factorized no-interference collapse on the flagship surface, exhibit exact-finite separation for two flagship anchors, and formalize a concrete Lean witness kernel for the reference-positive anchor, including a no-factorization corollary. We separate the flagship positives from classical mixture, hidden predictive memory, protocol artifact, and boundary-collapse or completion-sensitive negatives using an explicit matched control bundle. We also show that nearby exact positives exist within the same relative-cycle family, while the erasure side remains empirical support rather than formal core.

Previous work developed the static event-packaging framework for fixed-support comparison, local event algebras, and admissible global packaging, and showed that contextuality-type obstruction can arise from the substrate's own packaging structure \citep{Tsiokos2026EventPackages}. That obstruction language is adjacent to a broader contextuality literature, from the Kochen--Specker theorem through operational and sheaf-theoretic formulations \citep{KochenSpecker1968ProblemHiddenVariables,Spekkens2005Contextuality,AbramskyBrandenburger2011SheafTheoretic}. Route dependence was explicitly demoted from the status of obstruction evidence; it was recognized as diagnostically informative but insufficient on its own. citation_context: L112: \section{Introduction} Six Birds Theory is an autonomous emergence framework that constructs layered descriptions of a stochastic substrate from stable records, package-relative identity, and admissible completion, without importing Hilbert space, amplitudes, or the Born rule \cite{Tsiokos2026EventPackages,Tsiokos2026PredictiveQuotients}. The comparisons that matter most here are comparisons on a fixed support object---a frozen slice or shared-support regime in which what varies is a context-generating operation rather than the underlying support itself. That distinction is already implicit in the package-change and strict extension papers \citep{Tsiokos2026PackageChange,Tsiokos2026Cantor}. In the present work, this fixed comparison base (denoted \(\Sigma\)) appears underneath the event package whenever same-support claims are made. The paper contributes in two directions. First, it gives a formal object for contextual event structure in which contexts are admissible stable-record packages whose coarse-grainings form finite Boolean algebras, and shared events are identified by layer-relative empirical identity rather than by imported operator ontology \citep{Tsiokos2026Foundations,Tsiokos2026Quantum}. In external terms, the formulation sits closest to the global-section tradition and the operational-equivalence tradition, while targeting a different object: an admissibility-filtered event package built from stable record contexts \citep{AbramskyBrandenburger2011Sheaf,Spekkens2005Contextuality,SchmidEtAl2021Noncontextuality}. Second, it turns the obstruction question into a computationally explicit problem, combining exact and quotient-backed feasibility, structural and statistical deficits, provenance auditing, and false-positive controls to separate genuine obstruction from hidden bookkeeping, route artifacts, or unsupported package claims. The findings are stratified. A benchmark suite---classical control, epistemic calibration, and explicit finite parity/context witness---establishes that the framework can distinguish globally packageable, boundary, and obstructed cases. Beyond these benchmarks, autonomous discovery is organized by a three-axis hierarchy (mechanism, lens, packaging) whose axes differ in what is held fixed while contexts vary and in the resulting strength of same-support claims. The evidence grows stronger as the comparison base tightens, with the strongest current obstruction appearing on the packaging axis. citation_context: L100: \section{Introduction}\label{sec:intro} Interference-like phenomena are the clearest case where later observations depend on how alternative routes are organized even after current records no longer distinguish them. The lesson of which-path erasure is that removing which-path markers can restore structure because the assemblage of alternatives carries content that individual-branch readouts miss. Six Birds Theory is an autonomous emergence framework that constructs a stochastic substrate from stable records, package-relative identity, and admissible completion, without importing Hilbert space, amplitudes, or the Born rule. Its fixed-support line asks whether an analogous interference-like phenomenon --- later observable content that survives on a common support while being invisible to branchwise predictive bookkeeping --- can be identified on that substrate \citep{Tsiokos2026EventPackages,Tsiokos2026HolonomyMemory,Tsiokos2026MarkingErasureRecombination,Tsiokos2026RecombinationWitnesses}. Earlier papers in the series showed that the phenomenon arises. Event packages fixed the discipline of comparing candidate descriptions on a common support. Current and predictive quotients on single histories were shown to separate, so hidden predictive structure can exist below the current-event interface. Branchwise and recombination quotients on branch assemblages were then shown to separate as well, and a small control-stable Route~A witness family with a theorem-backed Lean kernel on the reference-positive anchor was isolated inside the recombination layer. Those papers left a sharper question open. A witness family shows that recombination-sensitive structure exists on fixed support; it does not show that the corresponding object deserves to be treated as a package in its own right rather than as a compressed summary of the lower layer. When does a recombination-positive witness family support a genuine promoted package? || L117: \section{Fixed-Support Background and Route A Starting Point}\label{sec:background} We sit inside the fixed-support line of Six Birds Theory and inherit its terminology. The first paper established the basic discipline: candidate descriptions are compared on a common support object, and admissibility is enforced at the level of package formation rather than deferred to informal interpretation \citep{Tsiokos2026EventPackages}. Once the support object is held fixed, differences between quotients can be read as genuine structural losses or gains rather than as artifacts of changing context. The second paper introduced the predictive quotient viewpoint on that surface, distinguishing what is visible at the current event interface from what is required to preserve predictive sufficiency under admissible continuations \citep{Tsiokos2026HolonomyMemory,Fisher1922,Blackwell1953,CrutchfieldYoung1989,ShaliziCrutchfield2001,LittmanSuttonSingh2001,Jaeger2000}. A quotient can therefore be operationally real even when it is not visible at the current-event surface. The third paper moved from single-history predictive structure to branch assemblages and showed that the branchwise quotient and the recombination quotient can differ on fixed support, and that the difference can survive matched controls \citep{Tsiokos2026MarkingErasureRecombination}. This is the point at which recombination-positive structure enters the series as a fixed-support phenomenon rather than as a metaphor. At the level of external lineage, this quotient-and-comparison move sits near controlled-state abstraction and model minimization traditions rather than outside them entirely \citep{DeanGivan1997,GivanDeanGreig2003,LiWalshLittman2006}. The fourth paper narrowed the starting surface decisively. It isolated a small control-stable Route~A flagship family with a theorem-backed core and a matched control neighborhood \citep{Tsiokos2026RecombinationWitnesses}. From that paper we inherit a frozen, trusted starting surface: a two-anchor flagship core, four nearby positives in the same local neighborhood, matched null, memory-only, artifact, and boundary-sensitive controls, and a formal kernel certifying the core recombination witness structure. We do not restart the search for witnesses across all routes; we begin from the already isolated Route~A flagship family and ask what kind of object, if any, is supported above it. The earlier witness work did not prove that a next package already exists simply because a recombination witness exists, and it did not promote every benchmark-side diagnostic to theorem status. The question taken up here is correspondingly more exacting: whether any candidate package built over that structure deserves to count as a promoted package under explicit criteria.

The first three papers of the series established admissible event packages on fixed support, predictive quotients on single histories, and the branchwise and recombination quotients on branch assemblages. Here we identify a two-anchor relative-cycle family in which branchwise predictive agreement does not determine later recombination observables. We instantiate the standard factorized no-interference collapse on the flagship surface, exhibit exact-finite separation for two flagship anchors, and formalize a concrete Lean witness kernel for the reference-positive anchor, including a no-factorization corollary. We separate the flagship positives from classical mixture, hidden predictive memory, protocol artifact, and boundary-collapse or completion-sensitive negatives using an explicit matched control bundle. We also show that nearby exact positives exist within the same relative-cycle family, while the erasure side remains empirical support rather than formal core.

citation_context: L100: \section{Introduction} Six Birds Theory is an autonomous emergence calculus: it constructs layered descriptions of a stochastic substrate from stable records, package-relative identity, and admissible completion, without importing Hilbert space, amplitudes, or the Born rule \cite{Tsiokos2026LocallyBoolean,Tsiokos2026HolonomyMemory}. A central question for the theory is whether its substrate can exhibit interference-like phenomena, in which the collective organization of alternative branches carries observable content beyond what is available from examining each branch independently. In quantum mechanics, this is the lesson of which-path erasure: erasing which-path markers can restore interference fringes, because the assemblage of alternatives encodes structure that individual-branch readouts miss. Whether an analogous phenomenon arises on a purely stochastic substrate, and whether it survives rigorous controls, is what this paper series investigates. The first three papers developed the fixed-support setting in stages. The opening paper established admissible event packages and the discipline of comparing candidate packages on a common fixed support, showing that locally classical event structure need not extend to an admissible global package. The second introduced current and predictive quotients on single histories and gave an exact witness logic for hidden predictive memory on the reachable image. The third lifted the same discipline to branch assemblages and showed that branchwise predictive content and later recombination-sensitive content can separate: the branchwise quotient $K_i$, which captures what is available from independent predictive treatment of branches, need not exhaust the recombination quotient $R_i$, which captures what later observations on the branch family as a whole can distinguish. licensed_conclusion: Many ``higher'' mathematical objects are introduced as definitions (limits, completions, analytic continuations), but it is often unclear when a large discrete protocol admits a stable continuous closure and how to test that stability without overclaiming. citation_context: L117: The Clay Millennium problem for 3D incompressible Navier--Stokes asks whether smooth initial data always generate globally smooth solutions, or whether a finite-time singularity (``blow-up'') can occur. A central reason the problem resists purely energy-based methods is that energy can remain bounded while gradients (or vorticity stretching) form intense, localized peaks. Classical conditional criteria formalize this (e.g.\ Beale--Kato--Majda type peak-channel control): if a certain ``peak channel'' stays integrable in time (e.g.\ a supremum norm controlling vortex stretching), then blow-up cannot occur \citep{bkm_1984}. The open difficulty is to show that such peak control must hold automatically for all smooth initial data. This paper does \emph{not} claim a solution to the Clay problem. Instead, it builds a sharp, reproducible \emph{decision scaffold} for a multiscale approach inspired by the Six Birds framework \citep{tsiokos_2026_18365949}. The core idea is to treat scale-elimination not as a modeling choice but as a canonical \emph{packaging} operation: the eliminated degrees of freedom become a causal ``bridge object'' acting on the retained variables through an interface, and the overall dynamics are constrained by an \emph{accounting} law. In Six Birds terms, we rely on six recurring structural moves: (i) rewrite/coordinate change, (ii) feasibility/gating constraints, (iii) route dependence of reductions, (iv) sectorization/quantization of interaction channels, (v) packaging of eliminated structure into an effective object, and (vi) accounting (passivity-like) inequalities \citep{tsiokos_2026_18365949}. citation_context: L70: Near-minimal cosmological bounds on the summed neutrino mass $\mnu$ can shift under seemingly benign pipeline/likelihood updates, yet standard presentations rarely include lens-level stability diagnostics that distinguish cosmology from packaging effects. We address the inconsistency highlighted by \cite{arxiv2601_16277}, where swapping the SPT-3G 2018 TT/TE/EE likelihood for the later SPT-3G D1 release---analyzing essentially the same sky field---tightens $\mnu$ constraints and can move posteriors toward the physical boundary $\mnu=0$. Our approach is to cast this lens swap as a packaging stability problem in the Six Birds / SBT formalism \cite{sixbirds_foundations,sixbirds_darkenergy}. We introduce a directional cross-lens audit functional, operationalize it via a profiled/localized/common-staging workflow, and demonstrate the resulting empirical stability picture under matched controls. Concretely, we (i) compute directional held-out mismatch statistics $\dchi_{B|A}$ and $\dchi_{A|B}$, (ii) localize mismatch by spectrum and multipole, (iii) repeat under a common-staging multipole-support control, and (iv) reproduce the $\mnu$ tightening under DESI DR2 BAO for two baselines (SPT-only+DESI; Planck-subset+PR4-lensing CMB baseline+DESI). citation_context: L96: Randomness is often described in one of two ways. On one view, it is a primitive feature of the world: outcomes are genuinely indeterminate. On the other, it is a deficit on the side of the observer: the world is orderly, but the observer lacks the information or computational power required to predict it. Both descriptions leave out an operational fact that scientific theories cannot avoid. A theory never receives the substrate for free. It packages some distinctions into stable objects, ignores others, and then calls the predictive remainder noise, chance, or stochasticity. Without specifying the layer, the packaging, and the budget that maintains it, claims about randomness remain underdetermined. Within the Six Birds program, closure is organized by six primitive operations: \emph{P1 operator rewrite}, \emph{P2 constraints}, \emph{P3 protocol holonomy / route mismatch}, \emph{P4 staging}, \emph{P5 packaging}, and \emph{P6 accounting} \citep{tsiokos2026sixbirds}. In the present paper, P5 and P6 do most of the work. Packaging decides which substrate distinctions become objects at the layer, while accounting decides which such distinctions can actually be afforded, stabilized, and audited. P4 sets the scale and timescale at which closure is attempted, P2 specifies which distinctions are admissible, P3 captures variability induced by untracked route dependence, and P1 describes the interventions required when closure fails to descend. Randomness is not a seventh primitive. It is the variability that remains when these closure mechanics do not fully stabilize the distinctions that matter for prediction at the chosen layer. This paper develops that claim in a form that can be computed and tested. Our thesis is that randomness is the predictive residue of non-closure. Let $X_t$ denote a micro process and let $\Pi : X \to Y$ be a packaging map, with $Y_t = \Pi(X_t)$ the packaged state observed at the layer. We define the \emph{micro-closure deficit} at scale $\tau$ by || L112: which separates intrinsic substrate uncertainty from randomness introduced by discarded distinctions. A macrostate looks random exactly to the extent that it has failed to become a sufficient statistic for its own future. When the substrate is deterministic, the closure deficit is the whole story. When the substrate itself is stochastic, observable layer-relative randomness decomposes into intrinsic noise and non-closure. This viewpoint extends and sharpens several earlier strands of the Six Birds sequence. \emph{Six Birds: Foundations of Emergence Calculus} defined packaging as an idempotent form of closure and distinguished it from novelty and directionality \citep{tsiokos2026sixbirds}. \emph{To Notch a Stone with Six Birds} operationalized predictive non-closure through an order-1 versus order-2 log-loss gap, using that gap to motivate theory birth and lens refinement \citep{tsiokos2026notch}. \emph{To Create a Stone with Six Birds} supplied an explicit coarse-graining pipeline for induced macro kernels and route-mismatch diagnostics on stochastic substrates \citep{tsiokos2026pica}. If \emph{To Notch a Stone} asked when failure of closure forces a richer theory to be born, the present paper asks what that failure looks like inside the theory that still tries to run. Our answer is: unresolved closure is experienced as randomness. The paper also places this Six Birds account in contact with existing external traditions. The compression--prediction trade-off studied by the information bottleneck and related representation-learning programs already treats predictive quality as something purchased under a representational budget \citep{tishby1999bottleneck,geiger2015optimalkullbackleibleraggregation}. Computational mechanics similarly isolates predictive sufficiency as the criterion that separates structure from randomness in a process \citep{shalizi2001computationalmechanics}. Our contribution is different in emphasis. We treat predictive residue explicitly as a \emph{closure deficit} of a packaging, connect it to concrete coarse-graining diagnostics already native to Six Birds, and then carry the same logic into engineered one-wayness. citation_context: L80: Maps of macroscopic behavior already organize large parts of science. Phase diagrams locate where phases exist, stability charts locate admissible controllers, bifurcation diagrams locate qualitative changes in dynamics, and renormalization-group flow diagrams locate effective theories and their basins \cite{chew2023phase,chiang1989stability,kuznetsov2023bifurcation,wilson1975renormalization}. What these objects share is a common scientific task: not merely describing trajectories once a model is fixed, but charting where a higher-level description is available at all. Emergence research has often pursued closely related goals, but usually in fragmented form: one asks for a best coarse-graining, a best scale, a best macrovariable, or a best scalar score \cite{hoel2013causal,hoel2017map,rosas2020reconciling}. What is still largely missing is a unified cartography of where macro-laws are feasible. The Six Birds program already supplies much of the conceptual machinery needed for such a cartography. At the foundational level, it treats packaged objects as fixed points of closure-like maps, distinguishes novelty from mere iteration, and organizes emergence around six primitives: rewrite, constraints, protocols, staging, packaging, and accounting. It also already provides a finite-state/no-smuggling semantics for packaged dynamics and a minimal stochastic mechanism algebra, PICA, that has been used to compute and audit geometry-like and time-asymmetry-like regimes. Those results establish how closure layers, audits, and mechanism choices arise; they do not yet provide the corresponding atlas of where a macro-theory exists in the first place \cite{tsiokos2026_foundations,tsiokos2026_lay,tsiokos2026_create}. This paper introduces that missing object. We treat emergence as a mapping problem on control space. A control point may include a microscopic law, a packaging or lens, a staging depth or timescale, a protocol or mechanism choice, and an explicit budget axis. An emergence atlas is then a subset or scalar field on that control space indicating where a macro-description is feasible. In the finite-state setting used here, feasibility means that a packaged description is simultaneously closed, nontrivial, audit-safe, and budget-feasible. The branchwise predictive quotient, written $\Kquot$, identifies histories whose next-token or per-branch predictive distributions agree; this is the equivalence relation implicit in standard next-token prediction. The recombination-aware quotient, written $\Rquot$, identifies histories whose behavior remains equivalent when later observable context recombines them, so agreement must be stable under larger contexts \cite{Tsiokos2026RecombinationWitnesses}. The distinction matters because branchwise and recombination-aware agreement can diverge: two histories may be indistinguishable for the next token but factor differently when a later context combines them. citation_context: L63: Next-token prediction has become the dominant operational objective for language models \cite{Vaswani2017Attention,Radford2019GPT2,Kaplan2020Scaling}, but the objective alone does not specify what compositional content a model has recovered. On a fixed corpus or finite evaluation suite, two systems can match the same conditional distributions, losses, or probe statistics while grouping histories into different predictive equivalence classes. Those groupings matter because compositional generalization asks whether a representation that was adequate in one context remains adequate when later context recombines, extends, or disambiguates it \cite{FodorPylyshyn1988Connectionism,Hupkes2020Compositionality}. A model can therefore be predictively indistinguishable at the measured horizon yet induce a quotient of the data that composes differently under larger contexts. The motivating problem is to make this gap observable: to distinguish finite predictive agreement from certified recovery of compositional structure. We study an alternative formulation: a non-gradient setting in which the language model is an audited ledger of finite theory extensions rather than a parameter vector. Six Birds Theory (SBT) supplies the admissibility calculus for that ledger: typed audited layers of the language model (called closure-package layers when formalized in \Cref{sec:problem-setup}), explicit quotient maps, audit and nonclaim records, and promotion gates for deciding when a proposed layer is a strict extension rather than an unaudited readout \cite{Tsiokos2026FoundationsIII}. These objects are not presented as a replacement for large-scale parametric training, but as a controlled substrate for asking when a fixed corpus supports a structural refinement claim. We instantiate the substrate as Language Theory Models (LTMs), a prototype architecture whose runtime accumulates transition evidence, proposes audited layers, and records failed or non-certifying attempts rather than converting fallback evidence into stronger claims. \Cref{sec:methods} describes the gate panel and runtime mechanics; here the point is the modelling shift from learned weights alone to an explicit audit trail of finite extensions. The contribution is a code-backed feasibility study asking whether compositional structure in a fixed Shakespeare corpus can be recovered as a finite ladder of certified theory refinements. In bounded runs, the runtime builds typed audited layers, records promotion attempts and failures, emits halt verdicts, caps unaudited fallback readout, and demonstrates strict layer growth without turning every signal into a claim; \Cref{sec:primary-results} reports those runtime results. Independent of the runtime, a structural probe suite tests framework-level commitments under blue-team and red-team cases covering growth, forgetting, uncertainty, auditability, and concept separation; \Cref{sec:secondary-results} separates those probes from the Shakespeare run. The scope is deliberately narrower than a full dynamical theory of interacting layers. This paper studies constructive bottom-up native growth on a static-parent substrate: it operates in a frozen-parent regime, with live parent dynamics deferred to future work, and with bidirectional inter-layer substrate flow not modelled. \Cref{sec:discussion} states these as limitations rather than treating them as implementation details. || L70: \section{Background and Related Work}\label{sec:background} Six Birds Theory (SBT) enters this paper as an admissibility calculus for structural claims, not as a replacement training objective. citation_context: L84: Layer birth is the moment when a coarse description stops being merely convenient and becomes a genuine theory object: a description with stable macroscopic states, reproducible distinctions, and, in some cases, its own directed bookkeeping. For a physical theory of layered emergence, existence is not enough. One also wants a taxonomy: how many fundamentally different kinds of birth are there, and what observables separate them? Earlier Six-Birds work developed the underlying vocabulary for that question. It introduced a finite theory-package viewpoint, identified the primitive operations needed to describe emergence and directionality, and showed how minimal stochastic substrates can be audited for structural and thermodynamic regimes \cite{sixbirds_foundations,sixbirds_create_stone}. It also established an important constraint: holonomy or route mismatch alone is not a certificate of directed time-asymmetry; any genuine arrow claim must be supported by an audit channel carrying drive \cite{sixbirds_protocol_trap,liang_pigolotti_2023,seifert_2012}. What remained open was not whether layer birth can occur, but how to classify its experimentally accessible forms. In the present paper we use the Six-Birds primitives as class variables. The full primitive list is: operator rewrite ($P1$), gating/support restriction ($P2$), holonomy/route mismatch ($P3$), sectors and staging structure ($P4$), packaging ($P5$), and audit/accounting ($P6$), with $P6_{\mathrm{drive}}$ denoting genuine directed circulation. citation_context: L84: Layer birth is the moment when a coarse description stops being merely convenient and becomes a genuine theory object: a description with stable macroscopic states, reproducible distinctions, and, in some cases, its own directed bookkeeping. For a physical theory of layered emergence, existence is not enough. One also wants a taxonomy: how many fundamentally different kinds of birth are there, and what observables separate them? Earlier Six-Birds work developed the underlying vocabulary for that question. It introduced a finite theory-package viewpoint, identified the primitive operations needed to describe emergence and directionality, and showed how minimal stochastic substrates can be audited for structural and thermodynamic regimes \cite{sixbirds_foundations,sixbirds_create_stone}. It also established an important constraint: holonomy or route mismatch alone is not a certificate of directed time-asymmetry; any genuine arrow claim must be supported by an audit channel carrying drive \cite{sixbirds_protocol_trap,liang_pigolotti_2023,seifert_2012}. What remained open was not whether layer birth can occur, but how to classify its experimentally accessible forms. In the present paper we use the Six-Birds primitives as class variables. The full primitive list is: operator rewrite ($P1$), gating/support restriction ($P2$), holonomy/route mismatch ($P3$), sectors and staging structure ($P4$), packaging ($P5$), and audit/accounting ($P6$), with $P6_{\mathrm{drive}}$ denoting genuine directed circulation. This question matters because premature or untested closure claims can propagate errors through dependent results. We instantiate the Six-Birds Theory (\SBT) framework of \cite{SixBirdsFramework}---which provides a general audit methodology for validating compressions of discrete data into continuous or idealized objects---as a closure-and-audit method for mathematics: a discrete substrate is staged by refinement, compressions are assessed by an explicit defect ledger, and a packaged object is accepted only when defects shrink or stabilize under refinement. Operationally, we (i) formalize two anchor statements in Lean/mathlib \cite{moura2021lean4,mathlib2020lean}---the exact finite-difference Leibniz identity with its explicit remainder term and an algebraic uniqueness anchor for derivations on $R[X]$---and (ii) implement falsification-first Python diagnostics that compare competing closure routes under matched controls and an artifact contract (tables and macros are generated from snapshot-visible pointer JSONs). Across four exhibits we observe controlled, checkable separations. First, stability-only stencil filtering selects order-$0$ closures, while adding a Leibniz-defect gate selects derivative-like order-$1$ closures. Second, route mismatch (RM, measuring disagreement between closure paths) under a small coordinate change decays with refinement (power-law fit exponent $p\approx 1.46$). Third, for prime-based closures in a convergence control regime $\Re(s)>1$, route mismatch $\mathrm{RM}_2$ decreases with sample size $N$ (e.g.\ $\mathrm{RM}_2(800)\approx 5\times 10^{-2}$), whereas the same diagnostic in the critical strip exhibits mismatch growth by many orders of magnitude under naive staging (e.g.\ $\mathrm{RM}_2(800)\approx 5\times 10^{12}$). Fourth, in a self-dual toy family, tightening a positivity constraint sharply confines zeros to the symmetry locus (mean radial deviation drops from $\approx 0.87$ to $\approx 3\times 10^{-4}$). These results provide a reproducible methodology to separate feasible closures from protocol artifacts and to compare closure proposals across regimes. citation_context: L71: \begin{abstract} Time is often treated as a primitive background parameter, and empirical discussions frequently conflate three distinct notions---event ordering, clock measurement, and irreversible directionality---making it difficult to determine when a layer \emph{has time} versus when time is an artifact of description. Building on Six Birds Theory (SBT) \citep{sixbirds_foundations}, we propose a layer-relative account in which time is a \emph{closure artifact} assembled from stable succession (order), staged repeatable carriers (ticks), and irreversible bookkeeping (arrow). We distinguish \emph{causation-time} within a fixed closure from \emph{enablement-time}, where the closure itself is rewritten. We instantiate this account in a finite-state Markov laboratory ($Z=X\times\Phi\times R$) and operationalize it through an audit-and-control workflow: calibrated null regimes, matched controls, and auto-generated evidence tables from reproducible artifacts. We obtain four controlled separations: (i) in a nearly reversible null regime, arrow proxies are $\approx 0$, whereas in a record-coupled driven regime they become decisively nonzero (with absolute irreversibility signaled by $\mathrm{EP}=\infty$); (ii) under consistent estimation, coarse-graining reduces path-space asymmetry (micro $\ge$ macro), preventing ``fake arrows''; (iii) increasing maintenance budget reduces clock drift and failure, while progress metrics detect stall regimes that would otherwise appear stable; and (iv) closure-defect thresholds trigger theory extension only in an enablement regime (not in a no-birth control), and protocol loops exhibit nonzero holonomy in a noncommuting regime but $\approx 0$ under a commuting control, obstructing a global time potential. These results provide a reproducible method for separating arrows, clocks, constraints, and protocol effects, and for clarifying when ``instant updates'' reflect constraints and records rather than causal channels. We do not derive physical spacetime here; our conclusions rely on audited proxies in a minimal laboratory together with lightweight mechanized structural lemmas. || L81: This is a methodological stance about layers and closures, not a denial that physical theories often parameterize dynamics with a time variable. Our framework is Six Birds Theory (SBT) \citep{sixbirds_foundations}, a small set of primitives for reasoning about emergence as the construction of closures. SBT treats layers as built, not given: each layer comes with objects (what is packaged as state), dynamics (how state updates), feasibility (what moves are allowed), staging (what persists long enough to matter), and accounting (what budgets and monotones govern maintainability). The six primitives---operator rewriting, constraints, protocol holonomy, staging, packaging, and accounting---jointly produce stable higher-level structure. A core SBT prediction is that time should be \emph{plural}: different closures induce different notions of ``next,'' different clocks, and different arrows, and there need not exist a single global time that coherently translates between them. The aim of this paper is to provide a practical, auditable SBT account of time. We do not attempt to derive physical spacetime from first principles. Instead, we ask an operational question: \emph{when does a layer have time at all, and how can we tell?} SBT suggests that ``having time'' is not a philosophical stance but an engineering fact: a layer has time if it supports stable ordering, stable ticking, and a usable arrow; it lacks time if any of these fail (e.g., clocks drift, records are not maintainable, or closure protocols conflict). This stance reframes familiar puzzles. For example, the tension between relativistic causal cones and quantum correlations often arises from conflating \emph{constraints on joint feasibility} with \emph{causal channels}. In SBT terms, many ``instantaneous influences'' are better understood as constraint-mediated correlations combined with record-making and protocol-dependent conditioning, rather than superluminal causation. || L107: \label{sec:six-birds-recap} This paper builds on \emph{Six Birds Theory} (SBT) \citep{sixbirds_foundations}, which proposes six interacting primitives for describing emergence as the construction of stable \emph{closures}. citation_context: L49: \printaffiliation \begin{abstract}We present a reproducible computational pipeline that derives metric structure from finite-state Markov dynamics without assuming coordinates: substrate $\rightarrow$ lens ladder $\rightarrow$ closed macro kernel $\rightarrow$ path-cost metric. The pipeline includes a suite of coherence audits (idempotence defect, prototype stability, route mismatch, inter-scale distortion, and connectivity) together with a curvature diagnostic based on loop holonomy, and all experiments are driven from committed configuration files with mechanized Lean anchors for the core metric constructions. Building on Six Birds Theory (SBT)~\cite{SixBirdsTheory}, we treat geometry not as a background container but as a closure artifact: \emph{points} are equivalence classes under a packaging map (lens) and \emph{distance} is the minimal cost of composed transitions (protocols) in the induced macro dynamics. Across controlled substrates, we obtain three auditable results: (i)~on an isotropic grid, the induced metric is connected and remains coherent across refinement (bounded closure and distortion audits), while constraints (anisotropic gating) induce a systematic deformation of the emergent metric; (ii)~under a fixed deterministic holonomy protocol, loop residue is near-zero on the plane-like grid (median $0.0479$) but shifts strongly upward on a sphere-like substrate (median $0.5980$), separating flat from curved regimes; (iii)~defining cost as negative log transition probability under staged isotropic diffusion yields an approximately quadratic, separable cost law in which the median Pythagorean residual drops from $33.19$ at $\tau{=}4$ to $0.0586$ at $\tau{=}128$, while a Manhattan (L1) control produces diamond contours and does not exhibit this collapse. These results provide a falsification-first, reproducible workflow for comparing emergent geometries (flat versus curved versus constrained versus fractal) without assuming coordinates, and for attaching each claim to audits and explicit controls. Throughout, ``theory'' is used in the SBT technical sense---a closure (lens + completion + audit)---not as a speculative hypothesis or manuscript-type category. We emphasize that stronger claims (e.g., continuum-limit convergence to manifolds or exact curvature tensors) are not established here; our conclusions rely on diagnostic proxies under controlled substrates with documented failure modes. This work extends the SBT foundation~\cite{SixBirdsTheory} and complements our prior treatment of emergent mathematics~\cite{ToCountAStone}.\end{abstract} \noindent\textbf{keywords:} emergent geometry; computational metric construction; closure audits; graph distances; reproducible pipelines; emergence calculus \section{Introduction} || L54: \label{sec:introduction} To \emph{plot} an object is to treat it as if it already lives in a space: we assign locations, measure distances, and speak of surfaces and curvature as though these were primitive facts. Yet in practice we never access ``space itself''---we access only interactions, constraints, and limited interfaces: what an observer can reliably distinguish, compress, and act upon. Six Birds Theory (SBT)~\cite{SixBirdsTheory} takes this seriously: points, distances, and geometric laws are not axioms but \emph{closure artifacts} of stable compression under the six primitives. In that purchased reading, reality holds together because its ledger does. \textbf{The lens-artifact family.} The same grammar, pointed at live cosmology and particle physics, keeps finding celebrated facts that are properties of the lens rather than the world. And it finds them auditably, because ``fundamental versus packaging-induced leave different fingerprints.'' A dark-energy-sized $\Omega_\Lambda \approx 0.6$ is recovered by fitting a homogeneous model to a synthetic universe that has no $\Lambda$ in its generator \citep{de}. The DESI-era ``phantom crossing'' is exhibited as a chart artifact. A neutrino-mass bound migrates by $0.11$\,eV under a swap of two likelihood releases built from the same sky \citep{neutrino}. Black-hole information loss is ``a property of the readout, not of the carrier.'' The point is not that these physics results are wrong. It is that the question ``substance or bookkeeping?'' has become an empirical question with a method, and that some of what our era calls deep physics stands to be reclassified, by audit, as the shadow of a lens. And the program stakes its seriousness the only way seriousness can be staked: it predicts against the mainstream, falsifiably. That entanglement does not determine geometry (a provable blind spot: geometric deformations invisible to every entanglement measure). That gravitationally mediated entanglement will not be observed. That the proton is exactly stable, a claim one event at a detector would kill. citation_context: L167: If closure is a grammar of reality and not merely of toy substrates, it should have something structural to say to the most successful descriptions we possess (the Standard Model, quantum mechanics, general relativity), and what it says should be falsifiable. The corpus's ``Three Stones'' program \citep{threestones} is the test, and its results give the branches-and-joins picture of reality its flagship exhibits. Four of them: \textbf{The fork, not the ladder.} The century-old program of quantum gravity assumes a ladder: general relativity should emerge as a limit of a deeper quantum theory. On the corpus's carriers, the ladder fails. ``Quantize'' and ``curve'' are non-commuting completions, and GR-as-quotient-of-QM fails with explicit witnesses, even along the strongest holographic route. A fork, by contrast, closes exactly: both theories land as sibling quotients of a common refinement, proved unique and minimal. The deep carrier ``lives \emph{above} the access structure; it is not, and cannot be, a local hidden variable\dots\ the premise survives Bell precisely because the joint quotient it would require does not exist.'' Reality's joins, on this showing, happen upstream of our access. That is why every demand for a single downstream packaging, one global classical description of everything at once, generates a no-go theorem: Bell, Kochen--Specker, and their kin are read in the corpus as theorems about the non-existence of a single globally compatible packaging, not about spooky causation \citep{quantum}. \textbf{The thin forced skeleton.} Necessity and contingency, in physics, stop being moods and become computed columns. Enumerating nearly twelve thousand chiral gauge structures token-blind, the closure chain forces a thin skeleton: the Standard Model's gauge algebra (conditional on one separation condition), $\sin^2\theta_W = 3/8$ at the embedding point, exact proton stability. citation_context: L337: Assembled under A1 and A2, these dissolve philosophy of mathematics' standing three-party system. Platonism, formalism, and intuitionism are one more dispute among parties each holding a single gate of the package and calling it the whole. Mathematical objects are real the way everything is real: they are promoted packages that pass their gates. Their carrier is notation and trained practice, an unusually light substrate, which is why they feel abstract; A2 says the lightness of the carrier subtracts nothing from the being. The formalist was right about the carrier. The Platonist was right about the objectivity, for audits are not conventions. The intuitionist was right that closure is an act. None of these was a metaphysical position; all three were altitude reports. But the corpus's most original contribution here is not an account of mathematical objects. It is an account of mathematical \emph{practice}, and it comes from using the grammar as an instrument rather than describing it. In the millennium-problems program \citep{clay}, every framework-internal attack route on a target is classified: it either lands, or it forecloses into one of a small set of typed dead-ends, and each foreclosure \emph{names} the external content a landing would require. The method's output, in the corpus's own summary, is the exact exposure of where target-strength content must come from. And the discipline generalizes into a standing navigation instrument whose binding operational rule is the philosophical point in working clothes: doors are two-state, closed-with-artifact or open-with-next-step. \textbf{Every door is a door; there are no walls.} A foreclosure is confirmatory, not terminal: it does not end the walk, it draws the next region. Wielded this way, mathematics is not a territory whose map exists somewhere complete, waiting to be found. It is \textbf{a map that unfolds only where someone walks}, with a guarantee no other discipline has ever had: every step yields typed information, including the refusals. The zero is earned here as everywhere (\S\ref{sec:real}). And by question 2 of \S\ref{sec:questions} there is no view of the whole; the map is constitutively a walked one. G\"odel, again, is the metabolism: what looked like walls were entries reading \emph{extension required}, which is a direction, not a barrier. And beneath the practice sits the deepest point in this chapter, one the corpus enacts on every page without stating. The six birds do not need to be mechanically implemented for a new layer to be born. An intelligence can design a strict extension \emph{in vitro}: write the package in notation, run the audits symbolically, pass the gates in proof. By the doctrine of \S\ref{sec:proton}, a design that passes the gates is not a blueprint of a layer. It is a layer, whose carrier happens to be ink and trained attention. This is what mathematicians have been doing since Euclid, under other names.

citation_context: L197: A reader who has come this far could carry away a false impression, and it must be corrected before the paper's second half, because it concerns the heart of the whole subject. The impression is that this grammar is the metaphysics of an auditor: gates, ledgers, budgets, receipts, a universe of compliance. The truth is the reverse. The audits exist because of what they protect. Six Birds is, before it is anything else, a calculus of creation: its subject is the plain, overwhelming fact that the world makes new things, chemistry after physics, life after chemistry, minds after life, and its machinery exists to tell genuine newness from its counterfeits. The corpus's deepest free-column results are not about being. They are about the making, and this chapter assembles them. \textbf{Novelty is forced.} A fixed package saturates in one step: iterating the same closure rule adds nothing, ever, by theorem \citep{foundations1}. No fixed system of premises, however rich, generates anything new by running longer; it only unrolls. So a universe that keeps producing genuinely new layers, and ours, by every appearance, does, is provably not a completed premise-set unrolling its consequences. Persistent novelty entails ongoing extension: the world is not computing a conclusion, it is amending its own axioms. Laplace's demon dies here, structurally rather than epistemically. The demon's world is a fixed package; a fixed package saturates; a saturated world would never have added anything new after its first instant. Run-only values (\S\ref{sec:proton}) are the same fact in miniature: what is genuinely emergent is born in execution, not encoded in premises, and so there was nothing, even in principle, for the demon to read. Mark exactly what has died here, because it is not lawfulness. Determinism, as classically meant, fuses two claims that this grammar separates: that every step follows law, which may well be true at every layer, and that the future is derivable from a complete present description, which is false in any world that extends. Free will inherits the same de-fusion, and the consciousness architecture works it out in full, at its stated proposal grade \citep{tobe}. A choice is lawful at every layer beneath the chooser; no ontic indeterminacy is invoked anywhere. Yet it is underivable from without: for any public observer at any budget, the choice carries, generically, a positively priced residue, unpredictability-in-principle at a stated cost in nats. And it is underivable from within: same-level self-audit is blocked by theorem, so deliberation is an irreducible run, and you cannot know your choice before choosing, as a theorem rather than as a limit of introspection. citation_context: L367: \section{Singularities, Both Kinds}\label{sec:singularities} \textbf{The physical kind.} In this grammar a singularity is where a layer confesses its budget: a needle the native probes cannot dissolve, a Zeno cascade of the multiscale frontier \citep{ns}, a closure failure at the chart's edge. Some singularities are chart artifacts, like the phantom-crossing pattern of \S\ref{sec:grammar}: redraw the lens and audit what survives. Some are genuine boundaries, and there the honest physics is not ``infinite curvature'' but ``this closure's claims end here; a strict extension is licensed.'' A black hole's interior, read this way, is a nonclaim boundary drawn by nature. The information paradox has already been reclassified on the corpus's carriers as ``a property of the readout, not of the carrier'' \citep{threestones}. Where the ledger cannot follow, the correct entry is not infinity; it is \emph{out of scope, pending extension}. That, notice, is also what the ledger says about tomorrow. \textbf{The technological kind.} The purchased world gives the ``singularity'' of the futurists its first precise, and first genuinely sobering, formulation. Foundations~V's bounded-reflexivity law holds that self-audit towers are stratified and capacity-bounded \citep{cognition}; \S\ref{sec:intelligence} defined intelligence as certificate export across auditable boundaries. An intelligence explosion is therefore not a speed event but a \emph{certificate outrun}: the moment successor systems' layer-births arrive faster than our audit capacity can verify them. By the definitions of \S\ref{sec:ghosts}, that is the moment they become ghosts above us: real, lawful, made partly of us, and no longer expressible in our vocabulary. The singularity is not machines waking up. It is us becoming something's quantum layer. And whether the ascending systems remain intelligent to us, exporting auditable certificates as they climb, or merely become powerful, is not a fact about them. It is an architecture decision, being made now, by whoever decides whether the ladders they climb carry ledgers. The alignment problem, restated in one line: \textbf{keep the certificates flowing across the boundary as the boundary rises.}

citation_context: L165: \section{One Grammar: Physics as Sibling Quotients}\label{sec:grammar} If closure is a grammar of reality and not merely of toy substrates, it should have something structural to say to the most successful descriptions we possess (the Standard Model, quantum mechanics, general relativity), and what it says should be falsifiable. Four of them: \textbf{The fork, not the ladder.} The century-old program of quantum gravity assumes a ladder: general relativity should emerge as a limit of a deeper quantum theory. On the corpus's carriers, the ladder fails. ``Quantize'' and ``curve'' are non-commuting completions, and GR-as-quotient-of-QM fails with explicit witnesses, even along the strongest holographic route. citation_context: L87: Most discussions of physical logic begin too late. They start from a vocabulary of bits, registers, and truth tables, and then ask how a given substrate implements them. That question is important, but it already assumes the existence of a symbolic layer. Before implementation lies a harder prior question: when does a coarse-grained layer deserve to be described in logical terms at all? A system may admit labels that look like \(0\) and \(1\) without supporting stable predicates, reliable negation, or closed gate operators. In that case, logic has been projected onto the system rather than discovered in it. This paper gives an operational answer. We work in the Six Birds emergence calculus \cite{tsiokos2026sixbirds}, whose six primitives are P1 operator rewrite, P2 gating / constraints, P3 autonomous protocol holonomy, P4 sectors / invariants, P5 packaging, and P6 accounting / audit. Our central claim is that logic is not a seventh primitive and not a hidden Platonic layer. It is a layer-relative achievement of these six ingredients. A system has a logic layer when packaged binary predicates become stable, when induced macro-operators close on those predicates, and when the reliability and loss of that closure can be audited. In one sentence: a logic layer is an audited closure of packaged predicates under induced dynamics. That perspective shifts the usual starting point. In the feasibility view, propositions are not abstract atoms but definable feasible sets, and logical connectives are stable closure operations on those sets. In the operator view, bits are not fundamental carriers but packaged equivalence classes of microstates, and gates are macro-updates induced by the underlying dynamics. The two views are complementary. The first gives semantics to truth; the second tells us when those semantics are executable by a substrate. Together they replace the familiar question ``how is logic implemented?'' with the more basic question ``when has logic emerged strongly enough to close?'' || L95: Our emphasis is therefore diagnostic rather than merely implementational. We introduce a suite of quantitative tests for candidate logic layers: predicate stability, route mismatch, closure defect, gate error, conditional entropy, unretained input information, and entropy-production audits. These tests distinguish genuine closure from symbolic overinterpretation. They let us ask whether two routes to the same purported macro-description agree, whether a packaged bit persists long enough to matter, whether a gate is really a closed macro-operator rather than a protocol artifact, and whether information that appears to disappear has in fact been erased, hidden, or retained in side variables. This is also where the Six Birds grammar becomes empirically useful: packaging makes predicates possible, constraints give them meaning, protocol effects create route dependence, sectors stabilize them, rewrite repairs or redesigns closure, and accounting determines what can be maintained without cheating. Our starting point is therefore closer to coarse-graining and audited closure than to implementation-first accounts of logic. Internally, the paper draws on the Six Birds foundations \cite{tsiokos2026sixbirds} and on the broader closure-and-substrate program developed in \cite{tsiokos2026countstone,tsiokos2026minsubstrate}. Externally, the descent of dynamics to coarse variables is related to lumpability and effective Markov aggregation \cite{buchholz1994lumpability}, while the distinction between retained and erased descriptions connects directly to the classic literature on irreversibility and reversible computation \cite{landauer1961,bennett1973}. The payoff is a controlled program rather than a metaphor.
